p: went up toward Jerusalem to war: That is, the second time: for in the first battle Ahaz was overcome.
David: Meaning, the kings house.
Ephraim: That is, Israel, because that tribe was the greatest, Ge 48:19.
moved: For fear.
Shearjashub thy son: That is to say, the rest will return which name Isaiah gave his son, to signify that the rest of the people would return out of their captivity.
firebrands: Which have but a little smoke and will quickly be quenched.
Tabeal: Who was an Israelite, and as it seems, enemy to the house of David.

sixty five years shall Ephraim be: Counting from the 25 years of the reign of Uzziah, at which time Amos prophesied this thing, and now Isaiah confirms that the Israelites would be led into perpetual captivity, which came to pass 20 years after Isaiah gave this message.
a sign from the LORD thy: For the confirmation of this thing that your enemies will be destroyed and you preserved.
tempt the LORD: Not to believe God's word without a sign, is to tempt God, but to refuse a sign when God offers it for the aid and help of our infirmity is to rebel against him.
men: You think you have to do with men when you contemn God's messengers but it is God against whom you bend yourselves.

himself shall give you a sign: Forasmuch as you are unworthy, the Lord for his own promise sake will give a sign which will be that Christ the Saviour of his Church and the effect of all signs and miracles will be revealed.
Butter and honey shall he eat: Meaning that Christ is not only God, but man also, because he will be nourished as other men until the age of discretion.
child shall know to refuse the: Not meaning Christ, but any child: for before a child can come to the years of discretion, the kings of Samaria and Syria will be destroyed.
Ephraim departed from Judah: Since the time that the twelve tribes rebelled under Rehoboam.
Assyria: In whom you have put your trust.
fly that is in the uttermost: Meaning, the Egyptians: for since the country is hot and moist, it is full of flies, as Assyria is full of bees.
bushes: Signifying that no place will be free from them.
feet: That is, that which is from the belly downward meaning that he would destroy both great and small.
nourish a young cow: He who before had a great number of cattle will be content with one cow and two sheep.
abundance of milk that they shall: The number of men will be so small that a few beasts will be able to nourish all abundantly.
bows shall men come there: As they who go to seek wild beasts among the bushes.
all hills that shall be dug: The mountains contrary to their will, will be tilled by such as shall flee to them for comfort.
